# Azure Mastery

> Azure Mastery is an iOS and iPadOS app for Microsoft certification exam preparation (Azure, AI, Data, Security, Power Platform, and GitHub). It uses on-device CoreML to predict your exam score (Exam IQ), build adaptive study plans, and track knowledge decay before exam day. 13,300+ practice questions cover 33 Microsoft certification exams. The app runs 100% offline with no tracking and no data collection.

Publisher: Moonbeam Alpha Ltd
Platform: iOS 18+, iPadOS 18+
Pricing: Free to download, with optional in-app purchases for full per-exam question banks. No subscription required for core study features.
App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id6760594569
Last updated: 2026-08-09

## Primary pages

- [Home — Azure Mastery](https://azuremastery.app/): Product overview, feature list, screenshots, and App Store link. Canonical entry point.
- [All exam pages](https://azuremastery.app/exams/): Hub listing every covered exam by family with links to each practice page.
- [Support](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/support.html): User support, contact, and FAQ.
- [Privacy Policy](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/privacy.html): Data handling — none collected; everything runs on-device.
- [Terms of Use](https://azuremastery.app/apps/AzureMastery/terms.html): Standard EULA for in-app purchases.

## Per-exam landing pages

Every exam covered by the app has a dedicated landing page describing the exam, the in-app question count, the official Microsoft Learn skills outline, a suggested study plan, and cert-specific FAQs. Question counts are extracted directly from the app's bundled question banks. Each page ships a single `@graph` JSON-LD block linking 6 entities (WebPage, BreadcrumbList, EducationalOccupationalCredential, SoftwareApplication, FAQPage, HowTo) for AI/AEO discoverability. The first 5 below are the most heavily-trafficked Azure exams and ship the deepest per-domain breakdowns.

### Azure infrastructure & solutions (7)

- [AZ-900 — Microsoft Azure Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-900/): 380 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: cloud concepts (25–30%), Azure architecture and services (35–40%), Azure management and governance (30–35%). Skills outline updated 14 January 2026.

- [AZ-104 — Microsoft Azure Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-104/): 612 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier sysadmin cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. Five domains: identities and governance (20–25%), storage (15–20%), compute (20–25%), virtual networking (15–20%), monitoring (10–15%). Skills outline updated 17 April 2026.

- [AZ-305 — Designing Microsoft Azure Infrastructure Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-305/): 400 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier solution architect cert (single exam earns the Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert credential). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions plus case studies. Four design domains: identity/governance/monitoring (25–30%), data storage (20–25%), business continuity (15–20%), infrastructure (30–35%). Recommended Associate prerequisite: AZ-104. Skills outline updated 17 April 2026.

- [AZ-204 — Developing Solutions for Microsoft Azure](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-204/): 405 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier developer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. **⚠ Exam retires 31 July 2026.** Five developer domains: compute (25–30%), storage (15–20%), security (15–20%), monitor/troubleshoot/optimize (5–10%), connect/consume services (20–25%). Heavy on SDK code samples in C#/Python/JavaScript. Skills outline updated 14 January 2026.

- [AZ-400 — Designing and Implementing Microsoft DevOps Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-400/): 470 in-app practice questions (largest single-cert bank). Expert-tier DevOps cert (single exam earns the Microsoft Certified: DevOps Engineer Expert credential). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions. Five DevOps domains: process/communications (10–15%), source control (10–15%), build/release pipelines (50–55%), security/compliance (10–15%), instrumentation (5–10%). Required Associate prerequisite: AZ-104 OR AZ-204. Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.

- [AZ-500 — Microsoft Azure Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-500/): 346 in-app practice questions. **⚠ Exam retires 31 August 2026** — successor is SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer). Associate-tier security engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates managing identity and access (Entra, conditional access, PIM), securing networking (NSGs, Azure Firewall, Private Link, DDoS), securing compute/storage/databases, and managing security operations (Defender for Cloud, Sentinel, Key Vault). Skills outline updated 22 January 2026.

- [AZ-700 — Designing and Implementing Microsoft Azure Networking Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/az-700/): 396 in-app practice questions. Specialty-tier network engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing/implementing core networking (VNets, peering, hybrid), private access (Private Link, ExpressRoute, VPN), routing and load balancing (Application Gateway, Load Balancer, Front Door, Traffic Manager), and securing/monitoring networks. Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.

### AI, Machine Learning & Copilot Agents (11)

- [AI-900 — Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-900/): 340 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired AI-900 on 30 June 2026 and replaced it with AI-901; AI-900 can no longer be scheduled.

- [AI-901 — Microsoft Azure AI Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-901/): 604 in-app practice questions. Current replacement for retired AI-900; the Fundamentals credential does not expire and local exam pricing varies. 45-min duration, pass score 700/1000. Two assessed areas: identify AI concepts and responsibilities (40–45%); implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55–60%). Requires foundational cloud/Azure knowledge and understanding Python examples. English exam updated 15 April 2026.

- [AI-102 — Designing and Implementing a Microsoft Azure AI Solution (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-102/): 334 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired AI-102 on 30 June 2026; the current role-based Azure AI apps and agents route is AI-103.

- [AI-103 — Developing AI Apps and Agents on Azure](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-103/): 557 in-app practice questions for the Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate credential. 100-min duration, pass score 700/1000. Five domains: plan/manage an Azure AI solution (25–30%), generative and agentic solutions (30–35%), computer vision (10–15%), text analysis (10–15%), and information extraction (10–15%). Requires Python and Microsoft Foundry experience. Skills measured as of 16 April 2026.

- [AI-200 — Microsoft Azure AI Cloud Developer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-200/): 444 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier AI cloud developer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing cloud-native AI applications, embedding LLMs into Azure-hosted apps, integrating with Azure AI Search and storage, and operationalising AI workloads. Skills outline updated March 2026.

- [AI-300 — Microsoft Azure ML Operations Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ai-300/): 400 in-app practice questions (covers the ML Operations Engineer role). Associate-tier cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates managing the ML lifecycle on Azure ML — model training pipelines, registries, deployment to managed and Kubernetes endpoints, monitoring drift, and responsible-AI evaluation in production. Skills outline updated March 2026.

- [AB-410 — Microsoft Intelligent Applications Builder Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-410/): 420 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cert with a 120-minute assessment for makers who build AI-powered business solutions in Microsoft Power Platform using Copilot, natural-language prompts, and low-code tools. Three domains: create a foundation for intelligent applications (25–30%), create intelligent applications (25–30%), and build business application logic and automation (40–45%). Microsoft's study guide was last updated 15 May 2026. Successor route for makers who previously targeted PL-200 — Microsoft replaced course PL-200T00 with AB-410T00.

- [AB-620 — Microsoft AI Agent Builder Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-620/): 452 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cert focused on designing and building integrated AI solutions in Copilot Studio. Three domains: plan/configure agent solutions (30–35%), integrate/extend agents (40–45%), and test/manage agents (20–25%). Official study guide updated 21 April 2026.

- [AB-731 — Microsoft AI Transformation Leader](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-731/): 352 in-app practice questions. Beginner-tier leadership cert (no-code), does not expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration (65-min seat), 30–40 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: identify the business value of generative AI solutions (35–40%), identify benefits/capabilities of Microsoft's AI apps and services (35–40%), identify an implementation and adoption strategy (20–25%). For business decision-makers, programme leads, and AI champions — not builders. Skills outline 2026.

- [AB-900 — Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-900/): 358 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 35–45 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: identify core features/objects of Microsoft 365 (30–35%), data protection and governance for M365 and Copilot (35–40%), basic admin tasks for Copilot and agents (25–30%). For IT admins deploying and governing Copilot. Skills outline published May 2026.

- [AB-100 — Microsoft Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect](https://azuremastery.app/exams/ab-100/): 421 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier architect cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates architecting multi-agent enterprise solutions with the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility framework, Microsoft Agent Framework, MCP extensibility, Computer Use, agent feed, and DSPM for AI. Skills outline published May 2026.

### Data (6)

- [DP-900 — Microsoft Azure Data Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-900/): 360 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates core data concepts (relational vs non-relational, OLTP vs OLAP), relational data on Azure (Azure SQL family), non-relational data on Azure (Cosmos DB, blob/file/table), and analytics workloads (Synapse, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI fundamentals). Skills outline updated 1 November 2024.

- [DP-100 — Designing and Implementing a Data Science Solution on Azure (retired)](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-100/): 350 in-app practice questions retained for reference. Microsoft retired DP-100 on 1 June 2026; it can no longer be scheduled.

- [DP-300 — Administering Microsoft Azure SQL Solutions](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-300/): 384 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier database administrator cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Five domains: plan/implement data platform resources (15–20%), implement secure environment (20–25%), monitor/configure/optimize (20–25%), automation (15–20%), HA/DR (20–25%). Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.

- [DP-700 — Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Microsoft Fabric](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-700/): 368 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier Microsoft Fabric data engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains each weighted 30–35%: implement and manage an analytics solution (Fabric workspaces, Git and deployment pipelines, OneLake security, orchestration), ingest and transform data (full/incremental loads, Dataflows Gen2, notebooks, PySpark, T-SQL, KQL, OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, Eventstream and Spark Structured Streaming), and monitor and optimize an analytics solution (alerts, error resolution, Lakehouse/Warehouse/Spark tuning). Requires SQL, PySpark, or KQL. Skills outline updated 21 July 2026.

- [DP-750 — Implementing Data Engineering Solutions Using Azure Databricks](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-750/): 408 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier Azure Databricks data engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Four domains: set up and configure an Azure Databricks environment (15–20%), secure and govern Unity Catalog objects (15–20%), prepare and process data (30–35%), deploy and maintain data pipelines and workloads (30–35%). Covers compute selection, Unity Catalog objects and governance (grants, row/column security, ABAC, lineage, Delta Sharing), Delta modelling and Lakeflow/Auto Loader ingestion, Spark optimisation (OPTIMIZE, VACUUM), and CI/CD with Databricks Asset Bundles. Requires SQL and Python. Skills outline updated 11 March 2026.

- [DP-800 — Microsoft Certified: SQL AI Developer Associate](https://azuremastery.app/exams/dp-800/): 364 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier SQL developer cert focused on AI-enabled SQL workloads (exam title: "Developing AI-Enabled Database Solutions"), renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration (120-min seat), 40–60 mixed-format questions, pass score 700/1000. Three domains: design and develop database solutions (35–40%) — advanced T-SQL, JSON, regex, fuzzy matching, graph queries, AI-assisted dev; secure/optimize/deploy (35–40%); implement AI capabilities in database solutions (25–30%) — embeddings, vector indexes, RAG with `sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint`. Skills outline published 12 March 2026.

- [SC-900 — Microsoft Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-900/): 408 in-app practice questions. Foundational exam, doesn't expire, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates security, compliance, and identity concepts; Microsoft Entra ID capabilities; Microsoft Defender XDR security solutions; and Microsoft Purview compliance solutions. Skills outline updated 7 November 2025.

- [SC-100 — Microsoft Cybersecurity Architect Expert](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-100/): 442 in-app practice questions. Expert-tier cybersecurity architect cert (single exam earns the credential, with prerequisite Associate cert). Renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 120-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates designing Zero Trust strategy and architecture, evaluating governance/risk/compliance technical strategies, designing security for infrastructure, and designing security for data and applications. Skills outline updated 27 April 2026.

- [SC-200 — Microsoft Security Operations Analyst](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-200/): 358 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier SOC analyst cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates mitigating threats with Microsoft Defender XDR (Defender for Endpoint, Office 365, Identity, Cloud Apps), mitigating threats with Microsoft Sentinel (KQL, analytics rules, watchlists, hunting), and managing security operations across the Microsoft security stack. Skills outline updated 16 April 2026.

- [SC-300 — Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-300/): 405 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier identity admin cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates implementing identities in Microsoft Entra ID, implementing authentication and access management (conditional access, MFA, PIM, passwordless), implementing access management for apps, and planning/implementing identity governance. Skills outline updated 27 April 2026.
- [SC-500 — Microsoft Cloud and AI Security Engineer](https://azuremastery.app/exams/sc-500/): 400 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier cloud and AI security engineer cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. The successor to AZ-500 (which retires 31 August 2026); beta from May 2026, exam expected July 2026. Validates managing identity, access, and governance (Entra ID, PIM, Key Vault, Azure Policy, RBAC); securing storage, databases, and networking (Defender for Storage, Azure SQL, NSGs, Azure Firewall, Private Link); securing compute and AI workloads (Defender for Servers/Containers, plus securing AI — Entra Agent ID, Defender for AI, AI Gateway for Foundry, Purview DSPM for Copilot); and managing and monitoring security posture (Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Security Copilot). Skills outline published May 2026.

### Power Platform (2)

- [PL-300 — Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst](https://azuremastery.app/exams/pl-300/): 365 in-app practice questions. Associate-tier data analyst cert, renews annually, USD $165 voucher. 100-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates preparing data (Power Query M, data profiling), modelling data (star schemas, DAX measures, calculation groups, row-level security), visualising and analysing data (Power BI reports, dashboards, AI visuals), and deploying/maintaining assets (workspaces, deployment pipelines, refresh, sensitivity labels). Skills outline updated 24 April 2026.
- [PL-900 — Microsoft Power Platform Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/exams/pl-900/): 351 in-app practice questions. Fundamentals-tier low-code cert, never expires, USD $99 voucher. 45-min duration, 40–60 questions, pass score 700/1000. Validates the business value of Power Platform, managing the environment (Dataverse, security model, ALM pipelines), Power Apps (canvas, model-driven and code apps, plus AI-built apps), Power Automate (cloud and desktop flows), and building agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio (topics, knowledge sources, MCP tools, channels). Skills outline updated 24 July 2026.

### GitHub (2)
- [GH-300 — GitHub Copilot](https://azuremastery.app/exams/gh-300/): 355 in-app practice questions. Intermediate GitHub certification covering responsible AI use, Copilot features (IDE, Copilot CLI, Agent Mode, Edit Mode, MCP, Copilot Chat, code review, org-wide policies), Copilot data and architecture, prompt engineering and context crafting, developer productivity, and privacy, content exclusions, and safeguards.
- [GH-900 — GitHub Foundations](https://azuremastery.app/exams/gh-900/): 367 in-app practice questions. Beginner-tier GitHub certification covering Git and GitHub basics, working with repositories, collaboration (issues, pull requests, discussions), modern development practices (GitHub Actions, Codespaces, Copilot), project management, privacy/security/administration, and the GitHub community.

## Guides

Free long-form study guides — exam-neutral advice grounded in the official Microsoft Learn skills outlines. Every guide article includes FAQ structured data, and the five how-to guides also include study-plan structured data. Index: [Azure certification guides](https://azuremastery.app/guides/).

- [Which Microsoft certification should you get first?](https://azuremastery.app/guides/which-azure-certification-first/): Decision guide mapping roles (IT ops, security, data, AI, business) to the right entry certification and its associate-level follow-on.
- [How to pass AZ-900 Azure Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-az-900/): Study plan, domain breakdown, hardest topics, and what to do after passing.
- [How to pass AZ-104 Azure Administrator](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-az-104/): Six-week study plan, domain weights, hardest topics (networking, RBAC), and exam-day tactics.
- [How to pass SC-900 Security Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-sc-900/): Security, compliance, and identity fundamentals prep with next steps into SC-500/SC-200.
- [How to pass DP-900 Data Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-dp-900/): Core data concepts, relational vs non-relational, analytics, and the data career path.
- [How to pass AI-901 AI Fundamentals](https://azuremastery.app/guides/how-to-pass-ai-901/): The AI-900 successor — AI workloads, generative AI, responsible AI, and the AI-103 path.
- [AZ-900 vs AZ-104](https://azuremastery.app/guides/az-900-vs-az-104/): Which Azure certification fits, whether you need both, and in what order.
- [SC-900 vs AZ-900](https://azuremastery.app/guides/sc-900-vs-az-900/): Security-first or cloud-first — how the two fundamentals exams differ and which to sit first.

## Core capabilities

- **Exam IQ**: On-device CoreML model that predicts your exam-day score with confidence intervals, using Item Response Theory (IRT) and Bayesian inference over your answer history.
- **Adaptive study plans**: The app picks your next session — weak-spot drills, knowledge-decay refreshes, mock exams — based on your current ability estimate per domain.
- **Aura first-week guidance**: Aura adapts the learner's next step throughout the first week and closes every study block with a concise, evidence-led recap.
- **Exam simulator**: Full-length mock exams under real timing and question distribution for each Microsoft exam.
- **Knowledge decay tracking**: Spaced-repetition signals flag topics where your retention has dropped before exam day, with targeted refresher sessions.
- **Question types**: Multiple choice, multi-select, drag-and-drop ordering, hotspot, case studies — matching the formats Microsoft uses on the real exams.
- **Answer Coach**: For incorrect answers, authored certification guidance explains the misconception, key distinction, and rule to remember. On supported devices, an optional on-device model may rewrite the note only when it passes grounding checks.
- **Offline-first**: Works fully without a network. No telemetry, no analytics on user behavior, no account required.
- **Apple ecosystem**: Native SwiftUI on iPhone and iPad; Live Activities for active study sessions; Apple Watch glance for streaks and XP.

## Differentiation

Azure Mastery is built for serious certification candidates who want to know *when they're ready* rather than just drilling questions. It is differentiated from generic flashcard apps by:

1. ML score prediction calibrated to Microsoft's pass thresholds, not a raw % correct.
2. Per-domain ability estimation — you see exactly which of an exam's domains is dragging your predicted score down.
3. Knowledge decay alerts so you don't lose old material while learning new domains.
4. Privacy-first computation — Exam IQ, Answer Coach, and study-plan generation run on-device; optional sync uses the learner's private iCloud account.

# Full detail per exam page

Everything below is extracted from each page's own structured data (FAQPage, EducationalOccupationalCredential, WebPage) and regenerated whenever a page changes, so it always matches the live site.

## /exams/ab-100/ — AB-100 Practice Questions — 421 Qs for AI Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Plan AI-powered business solutions (25–30%)
  - Design AI-powered business solutions (25–30%)
  - Deploy AI-powered business solutions (40–45%)
Q: How much does the AB-100 exam cost?
A: The AB-100 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. AB-100 is a senior architecture exam, so Microsoft rarely discounts it in free-voucher promotions; if a voucher is available via Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, grab it. The credential also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the AB-100 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft specialty and associate certifications including AB-100 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates (Foundry models, Copilot Studio features, Dynamics 365 Copilot), so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in agentic AI architecture work. Fundamentals certifications such as AB-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the AB-100 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. AB-100 has a low pass-rate publicly reported by candidates because it spans the entire Microsoft AI surface (Foundry, Copilot Studio, Dynamics 365 Copilot, MCP, A2A) — invest in the readiness gauge rather than rebooking blindly.
Q: How long should I study for AB-100?
A: Most candidates pass AB-100 after eight to twelve weeks of focused study, assuming hands-on experience with at least one of Copilot Studio, Foundry, or Dynamics 365. If multi-agent orchestration is genuinely new to you, plan for three to four months — the exam expects you to design end-to-end agentic-first solutions, not just describe concepts. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are at exam-ready — do not book until it shows roughly 740 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: AB-100 vs AB-620 — which agent cert should I take?
A: Different roles. AB-620 (AI Agent Builder) is the maker-level cert focused on building agents in Copilot Studio — topics, generative answers, knowledge sources, channels. AB-100 (Agentic AI Business Solutions Architect) sits above it: it expects you to architect multi-agent, cross-platform solutions that span Copilot Studio, Microsoft Foundry, Dynamics 365 apps, and Power Platform — plus ALM, governance, ROI analysis, responsible AI, and security. AB-620 first if you are building agents day-to-day; AB-100 if you are leading the architecture decisions across teams.
Q: AB-100 vs AI-103 vs AB-620 — how do the roles differ?
A: AI-103 is the code-first developer credential for Python and Microsoft Foundry agents. AB-620 is the Copilot Studio builder credential for integrated low-code agents. AB-100 is the architect-level credential spanning Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform. Choose the implementation credential that matches your role before moving into architecture.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-100 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AB-100 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 421 AB-100 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AB-100 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AB-100 practice test mode?

## /exams/ab-410/ — AB-410 Practice Questions — 420 Qs & Exam Prep (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Create a foundation for intelligent applications (25–30%)
  - Create intelligent applications (25–30%)
  - Build business application logic and automation (40–45%)
Q: How much does the AB-410 exam cost?
A: Microsoft Associate exams typically cost USD $165, but pricing, currency, and taxes vary by country or region. Check the price shown when scheduling AB-410 through Microsoft Learn before purchasing. The certification must be renewed annually through Microsoft’s free online renewal process.
Q: Does the AB-410 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AB-410 expire annually. Renewal is free through a short, unproctored online assessment on Microsoft Learn during the six-month eligibility window before expiration. Microsoft does not promise a fixed question count. Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the AB-410 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AB-410?
A: Allow four to eight weeks of focused study if you already build apps and flows in Microsoft Power Platform. Spend longer if Dataverse modelling, Power Fx, model-driven app design, or AI Builder prompts are new to you. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge helps you decide when to schedule the exam.
Q: AB-410 vs AB-620 — which builder cert?
A: Different surfaces. AB-410 is the Intelligent Applications Builder cert: you build Power Platform applications — Dataverse data models, model-driven and canvas apps, cloud flows — that consume agents, prompts, and AI models. AB-620 is the AI Agent Builder cert, focused on designing and extending the agents themselves in Microsoft Copilot Studio. AB-410 builds the application around the agent; AB-620 builds the agent. Many makers hold both.
Q: AB-410 vs PL-900 — which should I take first?
A: PL-900 first if Microsoft Power Platform is new to you. PL-900 is the Power Platform Fundamentals exam and stays conceptual — what Power Apps, Power Automate and Dataverse are for. AB-410 is the role-based exam where you configure the real artefacts: tables and relationships, forms and views, cloud flows, and AI Hub prompts. Makers new to the platform often use PL-900 as a foundation before AB-410.

## /exams/ab-731/ — AB-731 Practice Questions — 352 Qs for AI Leadership (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Identify the business value of generative AI solutions (35–40%)
  - Identify benefits, capabilities, and opportunities for Microsoft's AI apps and services (35–40%)
  - Identify an implementation and adoption strategy for Microsoft's AI apps and services (20–25%)
Q: How much does the AB-731 exam cost?
A: AB-731 is a Beginner-tier credential. The voucher is USD $99 in the United States; in the UK it is typically around £77. Microsoft regularly offers free vouchers via Microsoft Build, Microsoft Ignite, and free virtual training events, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for active offers before booking.
Q: Does the AB-731 certification expire?
A: No. AB-731 is a Beginner-tier credential and, like other Beginner-tier Microsoft credentials, does not expire — only Associate, Expert, and Specialty certifications require annual renewal. Once earned, AB-731 is yours permanently.
Q: What is the AB-731 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. AB-731 retake failures usually come from underestimating the strategy and governance domain — most candidates over-study Copilot product features and under-study ROI, licensing models, and adoption frameworks.
Q: How long should I study for AB-731?
A: Most business decision-makers pass AB-731 after three to five weeks of focused study, assuming working familiarity with Microsoft 365 and basic generative-AI concepts. AB-731 is a no-code leadership exam — you do not need to build agents — but you do need to articulate ROI, licensing models, responsible-AI principles, and adoption frameworks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready; do not book until it shows roughly 720 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: AB-731 vs AB-620 — which is right for me?
A: Different jobs entirely. AB-731 is the leadership credential — for business decision-makers driving AI transformation across teams: framing ROI, choosing between build/buy/extend, championing responsible AI, and running adoption programmes. AB-620 (AI Agent Builder Associate) is the maker credential — for low-code builders shipping agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio. Pick AB-731 if your job is to lead change; pick AB-620 if your job is to build. Many programme leads take both.
Q: AB-731 vs AB-900 — what's the difference?
A: Different audiences. AB-900 (Microsoft 365 Copilot and Agent Administration Fundamentals) is the IT admin's Fundamentals exam — admin centres, Purview governance, licensing, agent approval flows. AB-731 (AI Transformation Leader) is the business leader's exam — ROI, adoption strategy, responsible AI, build/buy/extend decisions, AI council governance. AB-900 administers Copilot; AB-731 leads the AI transformation. Programme leads sometimes take both for full coverage.

## /exams/ab-900/ — AB-900 Practice Questions — 358 Qs for Copilot Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Identify the core features and objects of Microsoft 365 services (30–35%)
  - Understand data protection and governance tasks for Microsoft 365 and Copilot (35–40%)
  - Perform basic administrative tasks for Copilot and agents (25–30%)
Q: How much does the AB-900 exam cost?
A: AB-900 is a Fundamentals-tier exam. The voucher is USD $99 in the United States; in the UK it is typically around £75. Microsoft regularly offers free vouchers via Microsoft Build, Microsoft Ignite, and free virtual training events for Fundamentals certifications, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for active offers before booking. Fundamentals certifications do not expire, so there is no annual renewal cost.
Q: Does the AB-900 certification expire?
A: No. AB-900, like other Microsoft Fundamentals certifications (AZ-900, AI-901, SC-900, DP-900), does not expire. Once earned, the credential is yours permanently. This is in contrast to Associate and Specialty certifications which require annual renewal.
Q: What is the AB-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. AB-900's Fundamentals tier means the questions are broader than they are deep, so most retake failures come from skipped Purview / Defender XDR content rather than M365 admin centre topics.
Q: How long should I study for AB-900?
A: Most candidates pass AB-900 after two to four weeks of focused study, assuming basic Microsoft 365 admin familiarity. If Microsoft 365 admin centres and Microsoft Entra are new to you, plan for six weeks — the exam expects you to recognise admin-centre objects (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams, M365), Purview surfaces (Information Protection, DLP, Insider Risk, DSPM for AI), and Defender XDR features. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready; do not book until it shows roughly 720 or higher.
Q: AB-900 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: Different scopes. SC-900 (Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals) is the broad Microsoft security overview — Entra, Defender, Purview, compliance, identity. AB-900 is narrower and more practical: it focuses on Microsoft 365 Copilot administration, with security and Purview coverage scoped to the Copilot / agent threat surface (DSPM for AI, sensitivity-label flow into Copilot grounding, oversharing in SharePoint). If you already passed SC-900, AB-900 will feel like an extension. If you are starting fresh and your role is M365-Copilot-focused, AB-900 directly first.
Q: AB-900 vs AB-620 — what is the difference?
A: Different jobs. AB-900 is the Fundamentals-tier admin cert: it expects you to identify Microsoft 365 admin-centre objects, Purview governance surfaces, and Copilot administration controls (licensing, usage analytics, agent approval flow). AB-620 (AI Agent Builder) is the Associate-tier maker cert: it expects you to build agents in Copilot Studio with topics, generative answers, knowledge sources, and channel deployments. AB-900 administers; AB-620 builds. Many M365 admins take both because real-world Copilot rollouts require admin governance and maker support.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AB-900 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AB-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 358 AB-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.

A: Yes - the exam simulator runs full-length AB-900 practice tests that mirror the real exam's question formats and timing, including interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

A: No. Microsoft retired AI-102 and the Azure AI Engineer Associate certification on June 30, 2026. The exam can no longer be scheduled.
Q: What replaced AI-102?
A: AI-103 is the current role-based route for developing AI apps and agents on Azure. It leads to the Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate credential and assesses Python, Microsoft Foundry, generative and agentic solutions, vision, text analysis, and information extraction.
Q: What happens if I already earned Azure AI Engineer Associate?
A: A certification earned before retirement remains on your Microsoft Learn transcript. AI-102 and its renewal assessment are retired, so the exam cannot be retaken or newly earned.
Q: Are AI-102 practice questions still useful?
A: Yes, as reference material for Azure AI services, generative AI, vision, language, search, and document intelligence. New candidates should study the current AI-103 outline and use its exam-specific bank.
Q: What is the current path after AI-102 retirement?
A: AI-901 is the current Azure AI Fundamentals exam, and AI-103 is the current role-based route for developing AI apps and agents on Azure. AI-102 content remains useful as historical reference, but new candidates should use the AI-901 and AI-103 outlines rather than planning an AI-102 certification path.
Q: What replaced the retired AI-102 and DP-100 routes?
A: Microsoft replaced the retired AI-102 route with AI-103 for Azure AI apps and agents, and identifies AI-300 as the replacement for the retired DP-100 data-science route. AI-103 focuses on application and agent development; AI-300 focuses on operationalizing machine learning and generative AI systems.

## /exams/ai-900/ — AI-900 Retired Exam & AI-901 Next Step | Azure Mastery
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Describe Artificial Intelligence workloads and considerations (15–20%)
  - Describe fundamental principles of machine learning on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of computer vision workloads on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of Natural Language Processing (NLP) workloads on Azure (15–20%)
  - Describe features of generative AI workloads on Azure (20–25%)
Q: Can I still take the AI-900 exam?
A: No. Microsoft retired AI-900 on June 30, 2026, so it can no longer be scheduled. AI-901 is now the exam route to the Azure AI Fundamentals credential.
Q: What replaced AI-900?
A: AI-901 replaced AI-900 on July 1, 2026. It remains the route to Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Fundamentals and adds a more implementation-oriented focus on Microsoft Foundry and Python examples.
Q: What happens if I already passed AI-900?
A: An Azure AI Fundamentals credential earned through AI-900 remains on your Microsoft Learn transcript. AI-900 itself is retired and cannot be retaken.
Q: Are AI-900 practice questions still useful?
A: Yes, as reference material for core AI, machine-learning, vision, language, and responsible-AI concepts. New candidates should study the current AI-901 outline and use the AI-901 bank for exam readiness.
Q: AI-900 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: AI-900 first, almost always. AI-900 is designed as the on-ramp to AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator). It takes a few weeks to prepare for and does not expire; AZ-104 takes two to three months and requires hands-on PowerShell and CLI knowledge. Most people pass AI-900 to confirm cloud is the right direction, then commit to AZ-104.
Q: Is AI-900 worth taking if I am not technical?
A: Yes — that is exactly who AI-900 is designed for. Account managers, project managers, sales engineers, and finance partners all sit AI-900 to qualify for Microsoft Partner Network roles. The exam does not expect you to write a PowerShell script. It expects you to explain concepts such as region pairs, the shared responsibility model, and when a hybrid cloud is appropriate.

## /exams/az-104/ — AZ-104 Practice Questions — 612 Qs for Azure Admin (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Manage Azure identities and governance (20–25%)
  - Implement and manage storage (15–20%)
  - Deploy and manage Azure compute resources (20–25%)
  - Implement and manage virtual networking (15–20%)
  - Monitor and maintain Azure resources (10–15%)
Q: How much does the AZ-104 exam cost?
A: The AZ-104 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. AZ-104 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the AZ-104 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including AZ-104 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the AZ-104 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-104?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with prior Azure experience, or longer if they are new to administration. Practise identity and governance, storage, compute, virtual networking, and monitoring in the portal and with Azure CLI, PowerShell, and Bicep so you can choose and apply the right administration method. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready.
Q: AZ-104 vs AZ-900 — which should I take first?
A: If you have less than six months of hands-on Azure experience, take AZ-900 (Microsoft Azure Fundamentals) first. It builds the conceptual map AZ-104 assumes you already have. If you have a year or more of practical Azure work, you can skip AZ-900 and go straight to AZ-104 — most hiring managers care about AZ-104 specifically. AZ-900 is often dropped from CVs once AZ-104 is on it.
Q: AZ-104 vs AZ-305 — which next?
A: Pass AZ-104 first. AZ-104 is the Associate-level operational cert; AZ-305 is the Expert-level architectural cert. AZ-305 assumes you already understand Azure operations (the AZ-104 material) and adds requirements gathering, capacity planning, governance design, and choosing between competing service options. Most architects hold both — AZ-104 to prove they have done the work, AZ-305 to prove they can design it.

## /exams/az-204/ — AZ-204 Retirement & AI-200 Next Step | Azure Mastery

Exam domains:
  - Develop Azure compute solutions (25–30%)
  - Develop for Azure storage (15–20%)
  - Implement Azure security (15–20%)
  - Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize Azure solutions (5–10%)
  - Connect to and consume Azure services and third-party services (20–25%)
Q: When does AZ-204 retire?
A: AZ-204 retires on 31 July 2026 at 11:59 PM Central Standard Time. Microsoft lists AI-200 courseware as the replacement for AZ-204 courseware, but AI-200 earns a different credential. If you want Azure Developer Associate, sit AZ-204 before retirement; already-earned certifications remain valid afterward.
Q: How much does the AZ-204 exam cost?
A: The AZ-204 voucher is USD $165 in the United States, with regional pricing. Only book if you can prepare and pass before 31 July 2026; the exam and Azure Developer Associate certification retire on that date.
Q: Does the AZ-204 certification expire?
A: The AZ-204 exam and Azure Developer Associate certification retire on 31 July 2026. Microsoft states that renewal assessments are no longer available after a certification retires. Already-earned credentials remain on your transcript, subject to their existing expiration date.
Q: What is the AZ-204 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. Plan retakes carefully against the 31 July 2026 retirement — a fail on day 1 plus two 14-day waits eats four weeks.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-204?
A: Most candidates pass AZ-204 after four to six weeks of focused study, assuming professional .NET/Python/Node experience. If you're new to writing against Azure SDKs (Cosmos DB, Blob, Service Bus, Functions bindings), plan eight to ten weeks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you're at exam-ready — do not book until it shows roughly 720 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: AZ-204 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: Take whichever matches your day job. AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator) is for sysadmins and platform engineers; AZ-204 is for application developers. They cover overlapping infrastructure (App Service, Functions, Storage, Key Vault) but from different angles — AZ-104 asks 'how do I configure X in the portal'; AZ-204 asks 'how do I call X from C# / Python SDK'. With AZ-204 retiring 31 July 2026, the deadline pressure may push it ahead of AZ-104 in your queue.

## /exams/az-305/ — AZ-305 Practice Questions — 400 Qs for Azure Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions (25–30%)
  - Design data storage solutions (20–25%)
  - Design business continuity solutions (15–20%)
  - Design infrastructure solutions (30–35%)
Q: How much does the AZ-305 exam cost?
A: The AZ-305 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. AZ-305 is the single exam required for the Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert certification — the predecessor pair AZ-303 and AZ-304 were retired in March 2022. The Expert-tier certification also requires annual renewal (free, online via Microsoft Learn).
Q: Does the AZ-305 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Expert certifications — including Azure Solutions Architect Expert (which AZ-305 unlocks) — expire annually. Renewal is free: a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain active in solution-architect work.
Q: What is the AZ-305 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. AZ-305 has a higher fail rate than AZ-104 because it tests design judgement (which service for which requirement) over recall — many candidates need a second attempt.
Q: How long should I study for AZ-305?
A: Plan eight to twelve weeks of focused study, even if you have already passed AZ-104. AZ-305 tests judgement more than recall — you are given a scenario and asked which combination of Azure services satisfies it. That style takes longer to internalise than the AZ-104 'how do I configure X' style. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are at exam-ready — do not book until it shows roughly 730 or higher with reasonable confidence; AZ-305 is unforgiving of borderline scores.
Q: AZ-305 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: AZ-104 first. AZ-104 is the Associate-level operational certification required alongside AZ-305 to earn Azure Solutions Architect Expert. AZ-305 is the expert-level design exam and assumes you already understand Azure operations.
Q: Do I need other exams alongside AZ-305?
A: AZ-305 is the expert-level exam for Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert. You must also hold Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate, earned through AZ-104. Passing AZ-305 alone does not award the expert credential.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for AZ-305 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of AZ-305 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 400 AZ-305 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does AZ-305 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an AZ-305 practice test mode?
A: Yes - the exam simulator runs full-length AZ-305 practice tests that mirror the real exam's question formats and timing, including interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

  - Implement an instrumentation strategy (5–10%)
Q: What prerequisite do I need for AZ-400?
A: Microsoft currently accepts either Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104) or Azure Developer Associate (AZ-204) alongside AZ-400 for DevOps Engineer Expert. Azure Developer Associate retires on 31 July 2026, and Microsoft has not yet announced a replacement AZ-400 prerequisite, so new candidates should choose AZ-104 unless Microsoft updates the credential page.

Most people pass AZ-900 to confirm cloud is the right direction, then commit to AZ-104.

Practise deployment and migration, identity and security, performance tuning, automation, and HA/DR across Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, and SQL Server on Azure VMs. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready.
Q: DP-300 vs DP-900 — which should I take first?
A: DP-900 first if databases aren't already your day job. DP-900 (Microsoft Azure Data Fundamentals) teaches the data vocabulary — relational vs non-relational, OLTP vs OLAP, the SQL-family service triangle, Cosmos DB API options — without expecting you to write T-SQL. DP-300 is the role-based Associate exam — it expects you to manage Azure SQL workloads in production: write queries, configure HA/DR, tune indexes, secure the data plane. Most candidates pass DP-900 in a few weeks, then spend two to three months on DP-300.
Q: DP-300 vs AI-300 — different data roles?
A: They cover different parts of the data stack. DP-300 is for administering Azure SQL workloads, including security, performance, automation, and HA/DR. AI-300 is for MLOps and GenAIOps across Azure Machine Learning and Microsoft Foundry. Neither is a prerequisite for the other; choose based on the role.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for DP-300 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of DP-300 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 384 DP-300 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.

A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.

  - Monitor and optimize an analytics solution (30–35%)

A: The DP-700 voucher is USD $165 in the United States — associate-level pricing. Cost varies by region; in the UK it is typically around £113. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Does the DP-700 certification expire?
A: Yes. DP-700 earns the Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate credential, and like all Microsoft associate, expert, and specialty certifications it must be renewed every year. Renewal is free: you pass a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn, available in the six months before your certification expires. This is different from Fundamentals certifications such as DP-900, which never expire.
Q: What is the DP-700 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for DP-700?
A: DP-700 is an associate-level data-engineering exam, so plan roughly four to eight weeks of focused study. You should already be comfortable with SQL, PySpark, or KQL before you start — the exam assumes hands-on experience ingesting, transforming, and modelling data. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you are at exam-ready — do not book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: DP-700 vs DP-600 — which should I take?
A: Both are Microsoft Fabric associate certifications, and your role should decide. DP-600 (Fabric Analytics Engineer) leans toward analytics: semantic models, Power BI, DAX, and serving data for reporting. DP-700 (Fabric Data Engineer) leans toward data engineering: ingestion and transformation with pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, notebooks and PySpark, real-time streaming with Eventstream and KQL, plus Lakehouse and Warehouse optimisation. If you build the pipelines that load and shape data, take DP-700; if you model and serve it for analytics, take DP-600. Many engineers eventually earn both.
Q: Is DP-700 a technical, hands-on exam?
A: Yes. DP-700 expects you to reason about real data-engineering work in Microsoft Fabric — writing and debugging T-SQL, PySpark, and KQL; designing full and incremental load patterns; working with Delta tables, OneLake shortcuts, mirroring, and pipelines; and optimising Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Spark performance. It is a working data engineer's exam, not a conceptual overview. If you want a non-technical, vocabulary-level data certification first, look at DP-900 (Azure Data Fundamentals) as an on-ramp.

## /exams/dp-800/ — DP-800 Practice Questions — 364 Qs for SQL AI Developer (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Design and develop database solutions (35–40%)
  - Secure, optimize, and deploy database solutions (35–40%)
  - Implement AI capabilities in database solutions (25–30%)
Q: How much does the DP-800 exam cost?
A: The DP-800 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. DP-800 is an Associate-tier credential and requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the DP-800 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including DP-800 expire annually. Renewal is free — a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain active with SQL Server, Azure SQL, and SQL in Microsoft Fabric. Fundamentals certifications such as DP-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the DP-800 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase. DP-800 retake failures usually come from underestimating the AI domain — most candidates over-study T-SQL and JSON functions and under-study embeddings, vector indexes, and RAG flows.
Q: How long should I study for DP-800?
A: Most candidates pass DP-800 after six to ten weeks of focused study, assuming working T-SQL fluency and basic awareness of embeddings and vector search. If T-SQL is new to you, plan for three months — the exam expects you to write CTEs, window functions, JSON shaping queries, and regex/fuzzy-match patterns from memory. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready; do not book until it shows roughly 750 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: DP-800 vs DP-300 — which should I take?
A: Different jobs. DP-300 is the Database Administrator Associate cert — running, securing, tuning, and recovering Azure SQL workloads (Azure SQL Database, Managed Instance, SQL on VM) including HA/DR, performance tuning, and automation. DP-800 is the SQL AI Developer cert — designing schemas, writing advanced T-SQL, and bringing AI primitives (embeddings, vector search, RAG, MCP endpoints) directly into the data tier. DP-300 administers; DP-800 develops. Many SQL pros take both because AI-enabled apps require both DBA discipline and developer fluency.
Q: DP-800 vs AI-103 — what's the difference?
A: Different stacks. AI-103 is for building generative AI solutions and agents with Microsoft Foundry, including model selection, orchestration, tools, knowledge sources, and operational readiness. DP-800 is for SQL developers bringing AI primitives such as embeddings, vector indexes, RAG, and structured outputs directly into SQL Server, Azure SQL, and Microsoft Fabric with T-SQL. AI-103 is application and agent-layer; DP-800 is data-layer.

  - Apply Prompt Engineering and Context Crafting (10–15%)
  - Improve Developer Productivity with GitHub Copilot (10–15%)
  - Configure Privacy, Content Exclusions, and Safeguards (10–15%)
Q: How much does the GH-300 exam cost, and how long is it?
A: The GitHub Copilot exam is roughly USD $99, though the exact price varies by region. GH-300 runs about 90 minutes and you need 700 out of 1000 to pass. It is delivered through Microsoft's exam platform, but the certification itself is owned and maintained by GitHub. Check the official GitHub Copilot page on Microsoft Learn for current pricing and any active promotions before you book.
Q: Does the GH-300 GitHub Copilot certification expire?
A: GitHub credentials are valid for two years and are renewed by re-examination — so once you pass GH-300 you stay certified for two years, then re-take the exam to keep the credential current. The certification is delivered by Microsoft but owned and maintained by GitHub, which sets this two-year validity.
Q: Who is the GH-300 GitHub Copilot exam for?
A: GH-300 is an intermediate-level certification for developers and technical team members who already use GitHub Copilot day to day and want to prove real, applied expertise. It assumes GitHub fundamentals and experience in at least one programming language. This is not a beginner exam — it validates working knowledge of Copilot's features, data flows, prompt engineering, and responsible-use practices.
Q: Does GH-300 cover using GitHub Copilot responsibly?
A: Yes. 'Use GitHub Copilot Responsibly' is the first domain, weighted 15–20%. It tests the risks and limitations of generative AI, ethical and responsible AI use, how to identify potential harms and their mitigations, and — critically — why you must validate Copilot's output before trusting it. Expect scenario questions about biased or insecure suggestions and how a professional handles them.
Q: How much of GH-300 is prompt engineering?
A: Prompt engineering and context crafting is its own domain, weighted 10–15%. GH-300 tests how you structure a prompt, how Copilot determines context, the difference between zero-shot and few-shot prompting, and the core principles of writing prompts that produce useful, relevant suggestions. It pairs closely with the data-and-architecture domain, which explains how your prompt is processed and turned into a suggestion.
Q: How many GH-300 practice questions does Azure Mastery include?
A: Azure Mastery ships with 355 GH-300 practice questions, each mapped to one of the six official GitHub Copilot domains — from responsible AI and Copilot features to data and architecture, prompt engineering, developer productivity, and privacy with content exclusions. Core study runs on-device and works offline; optional sync uses your private iCloud account.

Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready; do not book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.

AZ-900 (Microsoft Azure Fundamentals) validates cloud concepts and core Azure services. They are independent credentials in different product families — GH-900 is owned by GitHub and is valid for two years, while AZ-900 is owned by Microsoft and never expires. ## /exams/sc-100/ — SC-100 Practice Questions — 442 Qs for Cyber Architect (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Design solutions that align with security best practices and priorities (20–25%)
  - Design security operations, identity, and compliance capabilities (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for infrastructure (25–30%)
  - Design security solutions for applications and data (20–25%)
Q: How much does the SC-100 exam cost?
A: The SC-100 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-100 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-100 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-100 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the SC-100 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for SC-100?
A: Most candidates plan six to ten weeks after earning an accepted Associate certification. Focus on architectural trade-offs across Zero Trust, security operations, identity, compliance, infrastructure, applications, and data; practise explaining why each plausible distractor fails the scenario's constraints. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready.
Q: SC-100 vs AZ-900 — which should I take first?
A: If you have less than six months of hands-on Azure experience, take AZ-900 (Microsoft Azure Fundamentals) first. It builds the conceptual map SC-100 assumes you already have. If you have a year or more of practical Azure work, you can skip AZ-900 and go straight to SC-100 — most hiring managers care about SC-100 specifically. AZ-900 is often dropped from CVs once SC-100 is on it.
Q: SC-100 vs AZ-305 — which next?
A: They validate different architectural lenses. SC-100 is the expert-level security architecture exam, covering Zero Trust, security operations, identity, compliance, infrastructure, applications, and data. AZ-305 is the Azure solutions architecture exam, covering identity, governance, monitoring, data storage, business continuity, and infrastructure. Senior architects may hold both; neither exam is a prerequisite for the other.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-100 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-100 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 442 SC-100 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-100 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an SC-100 practice test mode?
A: Yes - the exam simulator runs full-length SC-100 practice tests that mirror the real exam's question formats and timing, including interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Manage a security operations environment (40–45%)
  - Respond to security incidents (35–40%)
  - Perform threat hunting (20–25%)
Q: How much does the SC-200 exam cost?
A: The SC-200 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-200 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.

A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-200 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. Q: How long should I study for SC-200?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with security-operations experience. Spend hands-on time in Microsoft Defender XDR and Microsoft Sentinel: investigate incidents, build KQL queries and analytics rules, hunt threats, automate response, and manage exposure. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready.
Q: SC-200 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?

Most candidates pass SC-900 in a few weeks then spend two to three months on SC-200.
Q: SC-200 vs SC-500 — different security roles?
A: Different angles on Microsoft security. SC-500 implements security controls across cloud and AI workloads; SC-200 runs detection, investigation, hunting, and incident response in Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel. Choose SC-500 for cloud security engineering and SC-200 for security operations.

Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Implement and manage user identities (20–25%)
  - Implement authentication and access management (25–30%)
  - Plan and implement workload identities (20–25%)
  - Plan and automate identity governance (20–25%)
Q: How much does the SC-300 exam cost?
A: The SC-300 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-300 also requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-300 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-300 expire annually. Renewal is free — a 25–30 question online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. Fundamentals certifications such as AZ-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the SC-300 retake policy if I fail?

Q: How long should I study for SC-300?
A: Most candidates plan four to eight weeks with Microsoft Entra administration experience. Practise identity lifecycle, authentication, Conditional Access, workload identities, application access, entitlement management, access reviews, and privileged access; use the portal and Microsoft Graph or PowerShell where the task calls for automation. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are exam-ready.
Q: SC-300 vs SC-900 — which should I take first?
A: SC-900 first if security and identity concepts are new to you. SC-900 builds the cross-cutting Microsoft security vocabulary including identity, but doesn't expect hands-on Conditional Access, PIM, or workload-identity work. SC-300 is the role-based Associate exam: it expects you to operate Microsoft Entra ID at scale day-to-day. Most candidates pass SC-900 in a few weeks then spend two to three months on SC-300.
Q: SC-300 vs SC-200 — different security roles?
A: Different angles on Microsoft security. SC-300 is the Identity and Access Administrator Associate cert — it focuses on operating Microsoft Entra ID end-to-end (identities, authentication, Conditional Access, workload identities, governance). SC-200 is the Security Operations Analyst Associate cert — it focuses on running Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel as a SOC analyst. They overlap on Conditional Access and Microsoft Entra ID Protection, but SC-300 goes much deeper on identity and SC-200 covers a broader detection / response surface.

## /exams/sc-500/ — SC-500 Practice Questions — 400 Qs for Cloud Security (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Manage identity, access, and governance (20–25%)
  - Secure storage, databases, and networking (25–30%)
  - Secure compute and AI workloads (20–25%)
  - Manage and monitor security posture (20–25%)
Q: Is SC-500 replacing AZ-500?
A: Yes. SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer) is the direct successor to AZ-500 (Azure Security Engineer), which retires on 31 August 2026. The SC-500 beta opened in May 2026, with full training and exam expected from July 2026. SC-500 keeps the core Azure security-engineering content of AZ-500 and expands the role to cover securing cloud and AI workloads — including Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Entra Agent ID, Microsoft Foundry, and Defender for AI. If you have not yet started AZ-500, most candidates should now prepare for SC-500 instead.
Q: How much does the SC-500 exam cost?
A: The SC-500 voucher is USD $165 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £128. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions during events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking. SC-500 is an Associate certification and requires annual renewal (free, online), so factor that into long-term cost planning.
Q: Does the SC-500 certification expire?
A: Yes. Microsoft Associate certifications including SC-500 expire annually. Renewal is free — a short online assessment on Microsoft Learn within the six-month window before your expiration date. The renewal targets recent skills outline updates, so staying current is straightforward if you remain broadly active in the role. Fundamentals certifications such as SC-900 are different — those don't expire.
Q: What is the SC-500 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for SC-500?
A: Most candidates pass SC-500 after four to eight weeks of focused study, assuming some prior Azure and Microsoft Entra experience. If cloud security is genuinely new to you, plan for two to three months — the exam expects hands-on knowledge of Defender for Cloud, Microsoft Sentinel, Entra ID, and Key Vault, not just concepts. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge tells you when you are at exam-ready — do not book until it shows roughly 720 or higher with reasonable confidence.
Q: SC-500 vs SC-200 — which next on the security track?
A: Different roles. SC-500 (Cloud and AI Security Engineer) is about implementing security controls — hardening identity, storage, networking, compute, and AI workloads across Azure and hybrid environments. SC-200 (Security Operations Analyst) is about running Microsoft Defender XDR and Sentinel as a SOC analyst, with heavier focus on detection, investigation, and incident response across the Microsoft 365 estate. If your day job is securing cloud and AI workloads, take SC-500. If it is running detection-and-response, take SC-200. Many Cybersecurity Architect (SC-100) candidates hold both, with SC-900 as the connective fundamentals.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-500 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-500 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 400 SC-500 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-500 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an SC-500 practice test mode?
A: Yes - the exam simulator runs full-length SC-500 practice tests that mirror the real exam's question formats and timing, including interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.

## /exams/sc-900/ — SC-900 Practice Questions — 408 Qs for Security Basics (2026)
Page last modified: 2026-08-09
Exam domains:
  - Describe the concepts of security, compliance, and identity (10–15%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra (25–30%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft security solutions (35–40%)
  - Describe the capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions (20–25%)
Q: How much does the SC-900 exam cost?
A: The SC-900 voucher is USD $99 in the United States. Pricing varies by region — in the UK it is typically around £77. Microsoft sometimes runs free-voucher promotions for events such as Microsoft Build or Microsoft Ignite, so check your Microsoft Learn profile for any active offers before booking.
Q: Does the SC-900 certification expire?
A: No. Microsoft Fundamentals certifications — including AZ-900, DP-900, AI-901, SC-900, MS-900 and PL-900 — do not expire. Once you pass, the certification is yours for life. This is different from Associate and Expert certifications such as SC-200 or SC-300, which require an annual free renewal assessment on Microsoft Learn.
Q: What is the SC-900 retake policy if I fail?
A: The first retake is allowed after 24 hours. Second and third retakes each require a 14-day wait. Microsoft caps retakes at five attempts per 12-month rolling period. Each attempt requires a new voucher purchase.
Q: How long should I study for SC-900?
A: Most candidates with prior IT experience pass after one to two weeks of focused revision. If cloud computing is genuinely new to you, plan for three to four weeks. Azure Mastery's readiness gauge will tell you when you are at exam-ready — do not book until it shows roughly 720 or higher predicted score with reasonable confidence.
Q: SC-900 vs AZ-104 — which should I take first?
A: SC-900 first, almost always. SC-900 is designed as the on-ramp to AZ-104 (Microsoft Azure Administrator). It takes a few weeks to prepare for and does not expire; AZ-104 takes two to three months and requires hands-on PowerShell and CLI knowledge. Most people pass SC-900 to confirm cloud is the right direction, then commit to AZ-104.
Q: Is SC-900 worth taking if I am not technical?
A: Yes — that is exactly who SC-900 is designed for. Account managers, project managers, sales engineers, and finance partners all sit SC-900 to qualify for Microsoft Partner Network roles. The exam does not expect you to write a PowerShell script. It expects you to explain concepts such as region pairs, the shared responsibility model, and when a hybrid cloud is appropriate.
Q: Is Azure Mastery free for SC-900 prep?
A: The app is free to download and includes a free allowance of SC-900 questions so you can try every feature. The full bank of 408 SC-900 practice questions unlocks with a one-time exam-pack purchase, or you can unlock every exam in the catalogue with a subscription or a one-time lifetime upgrade.
Q: Does SC-900 practice work offline?
A: Yes. Question practice, scoring, and the readiness prediction all run on-device, so you can study with no connection. No account is required, and your study data stays on your device with optional private iCloud sync.
Q: Is there an SC-900 practice test mode?
A: Yes - the exam simulator runs full-length SC-900 practice tests that mirror the real exam's question formats and timing, including interactive item types. Adaptive study sessions and Focus Weak Spots then target the domains where your accuracy is lowest.
